title: Trace Power Flow Across the Grid (DFS)
real_world_story: Field engineers trace a transmission path from a source substation deep into the network before backtracking to explore alternate branches. Depth-First Search mirrors this depth-first exploration of the power grid.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Substations and the transmission lines that connect them
real_world_connection.source_represents: The substation where the inspection begins
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Following one branch of transmission lines as far as possible before backtracking

problem_statement: Given N substations numbered 0 to N-1 and E undirected transmission lines, find the order in which substations are visited starting from a given source S using Depth-First Search. Process neighbors in ascending index order.
task: Return the DFS traversal order of all substations reachable from the source S.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and E. The next E lines each contain two integers u v describing an undirected transmission line between substations u and v. The final line contains an integer S, the starting substation.
output_format: Print the DFS traversal order as space-separated substation indices.

examples.explanation: Starting at substation 0, DFS moves to 1, then 3, then 4 before backtracking to explore 2.

expected_algorithm.name: Graph DFS
expected_algorithm.reason: DFS dives deeply along one branch of transmission lines before backtracking, which is useful for exploring the full reach of a connected network.

hint: Mark a station as visited when it is reached.
Recursively explore the neighbors of a station before backtracking.
Process neighbors in ascending index order for a deterministic result.
real_world_takeaway: DFS is a natural way to explore a network deeply along connected branches, helping engineers understand which facilities lie on each transmission path.
